lines: Think of the last prompt you typed twice. PromptVault gives it a home.
Can an editable decision brief help five more people in every hundred save their first workflow?
Here is the control. A new visitor starts with two empty fields.
Here is another visitor. Flagsmith assigned this one to guided templates.
Watch the end of the visitor ID. After the page refreshes, both the ID and the starting experience stay the same.
The guided editor already has a decision brief. I can give it a name that fits my project.
Opening the editor earns nothing. The first successful save queues a conversion under the ID that saw the starting screen.
Now I can fill the saved prompt with fresh release notes.
The Markdown export carries the reusable template and its input names. The notes I just entered stay in this browser.
For the demo, one click sends a hundred synthetic visitors through a separate Flagsmith client.
The simulator programs their chance of saving. Its receipt shows which events ingestion acknowledged.
These are results from the actual Flagsmith warehouse used for this recording.
Look at the number of exposed visitors in each arm before reading the lift. The inspector also includes a dated result that anyone can verify.
In the recorded example, control saved 28 out of 145. Guided saved 41 out of 156.
That is 36 percent relative lift, with an 89 percent chance of beating control.
The interval stretches from 22 percent worse to 94 percent better. Every visitor was scripted. The measurement works. The human question stays open.
